To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we derive optimal OSA policies for multichannel wireless systems, where the transmitter can probe channels to learn their state, and we present efficient suboptimal policies for the general case.
the optimal OSA strategy is a threshold policy and can be described in terms of an index policy.

the optimal channel probing and transmission scheduling policy for an opportunistic spectrum access system has a threshold structure with an index policy, that it can take one of three different forms, and that a dynamic program that solves for the optimal policy can be computed within a finite number (which depends on the number of channels) of steps, even in the case of uncountably infinite state spaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing optimal strategies for OSA in wireless networks.
the design of a spectrum access strategy for a transmitter in an opportunistic spectrum access network.
the problem of optimal opportunistic spectrum (or channel) access in a wireless communication system.

the optimal strategy has the following structure: 1) it has a threshold property, 2) it has an index property, 3) it can be described as one of three structural types, 4) it is computable by a dynamic program in finite time, and 5) it is suboptimal, but can be approximated by a look-ahead strategy that has a simple structure.

we have shown that the problem of finding the optimal strategy is equivalent to a data maximization and a throughput maximization problem and that both problems can be solved by a dynamic program in finite time.
the optimal strategy is computable in polynomial time and that a simple two-step look-ahead algorithm is optimal for a number (possibly infinite) of cases of practical significance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal OSA policy is characterized by a threshold structure and index policy, and can be computed efficiently via a dynamic program.
the two-step look-ahead policy is optimal in the case where the state of each channel is either good or bad and that the optimal strategy has a threshold structure for the more general case.

we have developed a framework for studying OSA problems, and have provided optimal solutions to two problems of practical interest, as well as suboptimal solutions that are shown to be near optimal for certain cases of practical interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in many cases of practical interest, it is sufficient to use simple, suboptimal strategies for channel probing and transmission scheduling in OSA systems.
, despite the complexity of the problems and the uncountable nature of the state space, the optimal strategy can be characterized by a simple index policy, which can be computed efficiently.
